title: 2001 HMMT February Geometry Problem 3
statement: Square \(A B C D\) is drawn. Isosceles Triangle \(C D E\) is drawn with \(E\) a right angle. Square \(D E F G\) is drawn. Isosceles triangle \(F G H\) is drawn with \(H\) a right angle. This process is repeated infinitely so that no two figures overlap each other. If square \(A B C D\) has area 1 , compute the area of the entire figure.

solutions.text: Let the area of the \(n\)th square drawn be \(S_{n}\) and the area of the \(n\)th triangle be \(T_{n}\). Since the hypotenuse of the \(n\)th triangle is of length \(\sqrt{S_{n}}\), its legs are of length \(l=\sqrt{\frac{S_{n}}{2}}\), so \(S_{n+1}=l^{2}=\frac{S_{n}}{2}\) and \(T_{n}=\frac{l^{2}}{2}=\frac{S_{n}}{4}\). Using the recursion relations, \(S_{n}=\frac{1}{2^{n-1}}\) and \(T_{n}=\frac{1}{2^{n+1}}\), so \(S_{n}+T_{n}=\frac{1}{2^{n-1}}+\frac{1}{2^{n+1}}=\left(\frac{1}{2}+2\right) \frac{1}{2^{n}}=\frac{5}{2} \frac{1}{2^{n}}\). Thus the total area of the figure is \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} S_{n}+T_{n}=\frac{5}{2} \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2^{n}}=\frac{5}{2}\).
